text:
sre-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on streaming inference path (service: runtime-streamer). p95=620ms p99=4.2s error_rate=0.8% — paging oncall

maria: oncall here, ACK. what's the window and which region?

zach: grafana window 10m, spike started ~3m ago, US-WEST-2 primarily. streaming stall count rising, tail queue depth on packer nodes up x6. link: https://grafana.internal/runtime/streamer?orgId=1&from=now-10m

lee: looking at packer traces — continuous batching task for streaming is accumulating very large batches (sizes 48-96) because seqlen mix has a lot of long requests, padding amplification causing per-token compute blowup and KV cache thrash. also seeing long GC-ish pauses in worker logs.

omar: confirmed in logs: many batches hit max_seq_len route > 3k -> blocking other small streaming requests. Can reproduce locally with mixed seq load.

maria: possible quick mitigations? we should aim to reduce customer impact fast.

lee: immediate options: 1) reduce max_batch_size for streaming pool from 96->24, 2) enable per-request batching exemption for < 1s latency targets (disable batching for streaming route), 3) tweak scheduler weights to prefer low-latency streaming queue over large-pack batches. I'd do #1+3 now.

omar: we can flip packer flag to prevent mixed-len aggregation: set PACKER_MIXEDLEN_THRESHOLD=2048 and PACKER_MAX_BATCH=24. patch via runtime flags on the nodepool.

maria: go for the fast config change. zach, can you apply?

zach: applying now to us-west-2 streaming pool — doing a staged rollout (2/6 nodes) to avoid secondary effects. command:```
# runtime-admin patch-nodepool --pool streamer-usw2 --set PACKER_MAX_BATCH=24 --set PACKER_MIXEDLEN_THRESHOLD=2048
```

ops-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.runbooks/streaming-tail-incidents — follow step 1-3 for live mitigation

zach: first 2 nodes updated, I'm watching metrics. p99 dropped to ~1.6s after first patch (20s post-change). continuing rollout.

julie-cs: what's customer impact? any >=P1 customers affected or 4xx/5xx spikes? need to notify CS if broad impact.

lee: currently errors are marginal — 4xx rate unchanged. affected subset: long-prompt customers and some streaming-heavy partners. I'd hold broad notify until we see p99 < 800ms.

maria: agreed. julie, standby for status update in 15m.

omar: while rollout continues, I'm enabling a temporary scheduler policy: give streaming route weight 3x vs batch-assembler in scheduler config. command:```
# schedulerctl set-weight --queue streaming --weight 3
# schedulerctl set-weight --queue packer-batch --weight 1
```

zach: weights applied. tail queue depth visibly dropping, streaming stall events trending down. p95 now ~480ms p99 ~720ms (2m post-weight-change).

sre-bot: NOTE: autoscale triggered +2 nodes in dedicated-streamer-pool as fallback (policy: emergency-scale).

maria: nice work. next actions:
- lee: prepare a short-term patch to skip batching for requests with seq_len > 2000 (queue-level guard) and open PR.
- omar: investigate GC/worker pauses and whether KV cache eviction is causing stalls; collect heap/kv metrics.
- zach: continue watch, roll remaining nodes if stable, post a summary in 30m.
- julie-cs: prepare customer note draft in case we need to notify impacted partners; include recommended retry/backoff guidance.

lee: will open PR referencing this thread, target hotfix branch. quick sketch in PR description:```
- if request.seq_len > 2000: route to non-batched low-latency executor
- enforce PACKER_MAX_BATCH override for streaming routes
```

omar: collecting GC traces now: `/srv/runtime/logs/streamer/*` and kv eviction traces. pushing logs to incident ticket.

zach: full rollout completed. p99 steady ~680ms over 5m window. no error spike.

maria: marking as live-mitigated. we should keep the incident open for followup engineering actions and a postmortem. filing incident ticket and assigning owners.

ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-0421 (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0421) — severity: sev2 — owners: maria, lee, omar, zach

julie-cs: thanks team, I'll hold draft ready. please ping me if we need to escalate to customers. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all. follow-up: lee will post short analysis + perf numbers, omar will post KV/heap findings, zach will close monitoring loop. reopen if regressions.

zach: note for postmortem: look at packer heuristics for mixed sequence-length workloads; maybe add dynamic batch-size governor based on seq_len distribution.

lee: will include those action items in the PM.

sre-bot: RESOLVED: live mitigation in place; continue to monitor for 2 hours before full close.
